decisions.statement: A path is read against the repository root rather than against the folder a call was made in.
An absolute path is resolved without the repository root.
A relative path is resolved against the repository root.
A path is answered relative to the repository root.
A path outside the repository is answered as no path.
One reader here answers no path for a path outside the repository and one answers that path.
A caller writing a render outside the repository reads its path by the second.
A path opening with `~/` is read against the home directory by that reader.
An absolute path that reader is handed is taken as that path is.
Any other path that reader is handed is read against the root handed with it.
The repository root is no path inside the repository.
The refusal for a path outside the repository is worded here.
A path bound for a write is weighed as joining that path onto the root leaves that path.
An absolute path a write joins onto the root is inside the repository.
A name opening with two dots is a name rather than a step out of the root.
A path reaching outside the repository through a symlink inside it is judged by nothing.
The refusal for a path written outside the repository is worded here.
The `.git` folder is refused.
A path under the `.git` folder is refused.
That refusal is worded here and is answered on its own.
That refusal names the sweep taking away what akasha left under that folder.
A folder at the top of the repository is refused.
A path with a `/` names no folder at the top of the repository.
A path the disk has no folder at is passed over.
Nothing here reads a file's body.
Nothing here writes into the repository.

definition: a path a command was handed, read against the repository root
